stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Sweep the three sliders and watch how each parameter changes the force of gravitational attraction between the two bodies. Advance once each slider has covered at least half its range.
stages.concept: Every mass attracts every other mass. Newton: $F = G\,\frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}$ with $G = 6.674 \times 10^{-11}\ \mathrm{N\,m^2/kg^2}$. Doubling either mass doubles $F$. Doubling $r$ divides $F$ by four.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: A target force $F^*$ is shown. Tune $m_1$, $m_2$ and $r$ until the live force matches the target within ±5%.
stages.concept: Many parameter triples give the same $F$. $F$ scales linearly with each mass and as $1/r^2$ with distance. Any $(m_1, m_2, r)$ satisfying $G\,m_1 m_2 / r^2 = F^*$ is a valid solution.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The force arrows are hidden. Only the target $F^*$ is shown. Compute $m_1$, $m_2$ and $r$ on paper first, then set the sliders. One submit per setup.
stages.concept: Inverse form: pick any two of the three parameters, then solve $r = \sqrt{G\,m_1 m_2 / F^*}$ (or solve for $m_2$ given $m_1$, $r$). Write the algebra, then set the sliders.

labels.tip1: sweep each slider across at least half its range
labels.tip2: align the live arrow length with the target arrow
labels.tip3: compute the parameters on paper first, then set the sliders
labels.peek_tip_formula: Rearrange: pick m1 and m2, then r = sqrt(G · m1 · m2 / F*).

1.1: Try changing only one slider at a time. Which one changes the arrow length most sharply?
1.2: Halving r roughly quadruples F. Doubling either mass only doubles F. Distance dominates.
1.3: To reach coverage, drag each slider slowly from one end to the other.

2.1: Read the target arrow length. Is the live arrow shorter or longer?
2.2: Fix r at a round value, then increase m1 or m2 until F matches.
2.3: Solve: r = sqrt(G · m1 · m2 / F*). Pick m1 and m2, compute r directly.

3.1: The pattern is hidden but the formula still holds. Write F = G · m1 · m2 / r^2 on paper.
3.2: Substitute the target F* and two chosen parameters, then solve for the third.
3.3: Numerical anchor: F [×10^21 N] ≈ 6.67 · m1 · m2 / r^2 with m1, m2 in ×10^23 kg and r in ×10^7 m.
